About this page

  • In this page we review the literature which document the development of Adela’s cfMeDIP-seq Technology. The source of all the information contained therein is public. The primary references are the following:1
1.
Shen, S.Y., Singhania, R., Fehringer, G., Chakravarthy, A., Roehrl, M.H.A., Chadwick, D., Zuzarte, P.C., Borgida, A., Wang, T.T., Li, T., et al. (2018). Sensitive tumour detection and classification using plasma cell-free DNA methylomes. Nature 563, 579–583.
2.
Wilson, S.L., Shen, S.Y., Harmon, L., Burgener, J.M., Triche, T., Bratman, S.V., and De Carvalho, D.D. (2022). Sensitive and reproducible cell-free methylome quantification with synthetic spike-in controls. Cell Reports Methods 2, 100294.
3.
Halla-aho, V., and Lähdesmäki, H. (2022). Probabilistic modeling methods for cell-free DNA methylation based cancer classification. BMC Bioinformatics 23, 138.
4.
Zeng, Y., Ye, W., Stutheit-Zhao, E.Y., De Carvalho, D.D., and Pugh, T.J. (2023). MEDIPIPE: An automated and comprehensive pipeline for cfMeDIP-seq data quality control and analysis. Bioinformatics 39, btad423.


1 AI Reports

  • AI reports are produced by claude.ai Opus 4.5 with naive prompts from Francois Collin.

  • The reporting done is intended to provide the information needed to understand the roots and development of Adela’s cfMeDIP-seq Technology.

2 Re-analysis

  • Two areas in the developmental path that are inviting to further study:

    • Spike-in Normalization and
    • Model Selection


2.1 Spike-in Normalization

  • Is all and only unwanted variation captured?: see Figure XXX

  • In the task of normalization, we need to counterweigh the desire to have unbiased estimates with the need to have low variability estimates.

    • the data need to be examined to see we are on the continuum.


2.2 Model Selection

  • Examine more model structures - enet, rf, pam, svm, gbm, knn, xgb
    • in addition to the error rate, we need to examine where the errors occur (samples) and how (miss by a lot or little)
    • compare validation and test error rates.


3 Extras

Home

DMA

  • Differential Methylation Analysis Methodology

  • Exhaustive survey of DMA methods used with each assay type.
    • Not specific to Adela
  • Describe the analysis data in each step
  • Survey of benchmarking studies and tools


Enrichment Based DNA

  • Enrichment-Based Differential Methylation Analysis

  • For enrichment-Based assays, a look at Bioinformatics Pipelines and Statistical Methods for Differential Methylation Analysis:
    • Common Bioinformatics Pipeline:FASTQ->BAN
    • DMA Methods for Enrichment based assays
      • many of the methods produce estimates of absolute beta, a measure of methylation level. These would then be further analyzed to get DMA results.


Variability in cfMeDIP-seq Data

  • The key components of the assay - filler DNA and antibody instance - are associated with a considerable amount of variability.
    • docname provides a detailed look at the Methylated DNA Immunoprecipitation Stage of the protocol.
    • questions to address:
      • how does the filler DNA operate? where does the variability come from?
      • how does anti-5-methylcytosine (5mC) antibody work? where does the variablity come from?
      • can variability be attributed to its proper source - anti-5-methylcytosine (5mC) antibody or filler DNA?
  • Rerun the analyses which assess the performance of the spike-in controls.
    • Wilson et al. (2022) [2]
